questions.question: What is the purpose of the Pose Classifier / Human Body Detection extension?
options: To detect human skeletons, joint coordinates, and track body postures using cameras
questions.explanation: Correct! Body detection tracks human joint coordinates (head, shoulders, elbows, knees) skeleton configurations.

questions.question: Which body joint coordinate represents the center of a player's head?
questions.explanation: Excellent! The Nose landmark represents the center of the head, ideal for placing funny virtual hats.

questions.question: How can you build a 'Body-Part-Counter' (like counting physical push-ups or squats)?
options: By checking if joint Y-coordinates cycle below and above a threshold boundary in a loop
questions.explanation: Perfect! Tracking Y coordinate peaks of joint coordinates automates physical exercise counters.

questions.question: How does Hand Pose detection differ from general body posture tracking?
options: It focuses specifically on tracking hands, palms, and 21 detailed finger coordinate joints!
questions.explanation: Spot on! Hand pose trackers map 21 detailed landmarks on palms and fingers for precise gesture inputs.

questions.question: Which finger coordinate represents the absolute top tip of your pointing finger?
questions.explanation: Great! The index finger tip landmark tracks pointing gestures, ideal for hover coordinates.

questions.question: If you want a pointer sprite to follow your hand tip, what block coordinates should you set inside a forever loop?
options: go to X(get hand X) Y(get hand Y)
questions.explanation: Perfect! Moving the sprite to hand X and Y coordinates binds it to your finger movement on the video feed.

questions.question: How can you trigger a virtual click event using hand gestures?
options: Checking if the distance between thumb tip and index tip is extremely close (detecting a pinch gesture)
questions.explanation: Spot on! Measuring finger-tip proximity (pinch checks) serves as an interactive air click trigger.

questions.question: Which block is called to start analyzing camera frames for body skeletons?
questions.explanation: Great! 'analyze body pose' triggers the skeletal tracking algorithm on the active frame.

questions.question: What happens if a skeletal joint coordinate is not visible to the webcam?
options: The AI returns low confidence coordinates or waits until the joint is visible again
questions.explanation: Excellent! The AI coordinates rely on visibility; low confidence coordinates are ignored to prevent erratic jumps.

questions.question: In a Clown Maker app, what block script anchors a virtual red nose sprite to your face?
options: go to X(get skeleton Nose X) Y(get skeleton Nose Y)
questions.explanation: Perfect! Centering the nose sprite on the Nose skeletal landmark creates a funny clown face overlay!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to analyze body pose and position a hat sprite at the coordinates of the 'Nose' joint skeleton.
questions.task_hint: analyze body pose -> set 3D position X(get skeleton Nose X) Y(get skeleton Nose Y) Z(0)
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Placing filters at joint skeleton landmarks anchors props realistically in real-time!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to track hand pose and place the cursor sprite at the Index Finger Tip coordinate.
questions.task_hint: analyze hand pose -> go to X(get hand landmark Index Finger Tip X) Y(get hand landmark Index Finger Tip Y)
questions.explanation: Perfect! This simple linkage creates a fully interactive virtual mouse pointer!
